newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: ANTI-EUTHANASIA GROUP SAYS DEATH A TRAGEDY
An organisation opposed to voluntary euthanasia says it's a tragedy that a South Australian woman took her life.

The National Coalition for Voluntary Euthanasia's, Professor Peter Baume, has confirmed that 52-year-old cancer sufferer, Janet Mills, died from a machine-delivered lethal injection, on January the second.
She becomes the second person to die in accordance with the Territory's Rights of the Terminally Ill Act.
The spokesperson for Euthanasia No, Tony Burke, says the Territory doesn't offer the good quality palliative care that could ease suffering for people with terminal illnesses.
Meanwhile, Northern Territory Chief Minister Shane Stone has refused to comment on the death of Janet Mills.
COALITION SAYS EUTHANASIA WOMAN'S SUFFERING INCREASED

The National Coalition for Voluntary Euthanasia says the suffering of a woman who's become the second person to die under the Northern Territory's Right To Die law, was increased by the law's requirement for a third signature from a specialist.
The Coalition's Professor Peter Baume has confirmed a statement on the Internet, that 52-year-old cancer sufferer Janet Mills died from a machine-delivered lethal injection, on January the second.
Mrs Mills made a public appeal in Darwin last month for a crucial signature of a Northern Territory cancer specialist to allow her to use the law.
Professor Baume says Janet Mills' suffering was increased by the hurdle of getting that third signature, which under the regulations must be from a Territory specialist.
He wants regulations eased to make it easier for people to use the laws.
GLIDER CRASH INVESTIGATIONS TO CONTINUE
Investigations will continue this morning into a crash involving two gliders yesterday at Tocumwal on the NSW-Victoria border, which claimed the lives of three people

A Swiss man, aged 30, who was holidaying in Australia, was completing a five hour flight in a solo glider, while a Tocumwal man, aged 42, and a woman aged 25, from Sunbury in Victoria, were completing a short training flight in the other glider.
Police believe they were both coming in to land at the Tocumwal airstrip when they collided mid-air, just after half-past-five.
The names of the three haven't been released.
PLANET ARK WANTS XMAS CARDS
Environment group Planet Ark says today is a day when Christmas cards are traditionally taken down, and says it wants your cards.
Today is the twelth day since Christmas and the group's hoping to start 1997 with a greeting card recycling campaign.
Executive Director John Dee says Australians sent more than 260-million cards and envelopes over the Christmas period, and he hopes to recover many of those.
He says people can return their cards at Coles, Video Ezy, and The Body Shop outlets around the country.
ANOTHER SEARCH FOR YACHTSMEN OFF AUSTRALIAN COAST
An RAAF Orian with about 15 people on board has left Adelaide to search for two round-the-world sailors.
The airforce says it believes they have had to leave their vessels in treacherous sea in the Southern Ocean off Western Australia.
Distress signals were received from the two yachts early this morning, and the airforce believes the vessels are around 14-hundred nautical miles south-west of Perth.
That's around the same area where a French sailor recently had to be rescued.
Wing Commander Ian Pearson says says one of the sailors is understood to be French, while it appears the other may be British.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
